rationales: The covalent radius, often called atomic radius in this context, is half the internuclear distance between two identical bonded atoms.
Atomic size is a general term and is not the specific term requested.
An ionic bond is a type of chemical bond, not a measure of atomic distance.
Ionization energy is the energy needed to remove an electron from an atom.
Sodium chloride is soluble in water.
Potassium bromide is soluble in water.
Benzene (C₆H₆) is nonpolar and insoluble in water.
Magnesium chloride is soluble in water.
0.03% is not the stated chlorine proportion in ocean water.
0.9% is not the stated chlorine proportion in ocean water.
7.8% is not the stated chlorine proportion in ocean water.
The textbook value for chlorine in ocean water is about 1.8%.
Density is mass per unit volume, not moles of solute per dm³.
Percentage expresses a component as a fraction of the whole, usually multiplied by 100.
Molarity is the number of moles of solute per dm³ of solution.
Dilution is the process of reducing a solution's concentration.
Melting changes a solid into a liquid.
Evaporation changes a liquid into a gas.
Condensation changes a gas into a liquid.
Freezing changes a liquid into a solid.
An ionic bond forms through electron transfer rather than equal sharing.
A coordinate bond forms when both shared electrons are donated by one atom.
System energy is not a type of chemical bond.
Equal sharing between identical atoms forms a pure covalent bond.
Milk is a colloid and is classified as a heterogeneous mixture.
Ink is generally treated as a homogeneous mixture in this classification.
Milk of magnesia is a suspension and is also a heterogeneous mixture, so this is another valid option.
Sugar solution is a homogeneous mixture.
450 °C is far below sodium chloride's melting point.
1413 °C is not the melting point; it is near the boiling-point range.
Sodium chloride melts at about 801 °C, which rounds to 800 °C.
1000 °C is higher than sodium chloride's melting point.
2.7 is below fluorine's electronegativity on the Pauling scale.
3.0 is below fluorine's electronegativity on the Pauling scale.
3.2 is below fluorine's electronegativity on the Pauling scale.
Fluorine has an electronegativity of about 4.0 on the Pauling scale.
160 pm is smaller than the commonly listed atomic radius of sodium.
162 pm is smaller than the commonly listed atomic radius of sodium.
185 pm is close but not the standard value given for sodium's atomic size.
The commonly listed atomic size of sodium is 186 pm.
Carbon-12 makes up about 98.9% of naturally occurring carbon.
96.6% is below the natural abundance of carbon-12.
99.7% is above the natural abundance of carbon-12.
97.6% is below the natural abundance of carbon-12.
Chlorine has more than one electron in its valence shell.
Chlorine has more than two electrons in its valence shell.
Chlorine has more than five electrons in its valence shell.
Chlorine has seven valence electrons, as shown by its electron configuration 2, 8, 7.
H₂O contains three atoms per molecule.
H₂ contains only two atoms per molecule, so it is not triatomic.
O₃ contains three atoms per molecule.
CO₂ contains three atoms per molecule.
Electrons are not the characteristic products of U-235 fission.
Protons are not the characteristic products of U-235 fission.
U-235 fission typically releases neutrons along with the fission fragments.
Potassium is not a general product of U-235 fission.
Mendeleev did not arrange his table by electronic configuration.
Mendeleev arranged elements primarily in order of increasing atomic mass.
Atomic number was the basis of the later modern periodic table, not Mendeleev's original table.
Completion of subshells was not the basis of Mendeleev's arrangement.
